$comment: ADG NTFS collector targets. Copy to adg-ntfs-targets.json and edit.
This file holds NO credentials. Collection runs as the identity of the process - a group
managed service account in production - so that no password exists to store or leak.
Scan roots are explicit: ADG never sweeps an estate it was not pointed at. Generate this
list from ADG's own share inventory (GET /api/v1/servers/{server}/shares) rather than by
probing, and keep it under change control alongside the rest of your configuration.
$comment_roots: A scan root may be a share root or any directory inside one. Starting below a share root
is cheaper and it costs something: the starting directory's parent is not read, so its
boundary is reported as 'scan_root' - unknown, and therefore a boundary - rather than
compared against anything, and the run cannot reconcile the share's tree.
shareRoots is still accepted as a spelling of this field, so a Phase 3A configuration
One root may not sit inside another: both runs would read the same subtree, and report
it as a compared directory in one and a scan_root boundary in the other.
$comment_batchSize: Observations per batch. The contract's ceiling is 1000. A resource observation and all of its ACEs always travel in one batch, so a batch may exceed this slightly rather than split a DACL - the server can only verify a reported acl_hash against a complete one.
$comment_maxDepth: How many levels below a scan root to walk. 0 reads the roots and nothing else. The default of 64 is past any tree a file server holds in practice; it exists so that a misconfiguration cannot become a walk that never ends. Reaching the limit is reported as an error and stops that tree from being reconciled, so a limit that was actually hit is never mistaken for a tree that ended.
$comment_excludePaths: UNC path patterns whose directories and subtrees are not read at all. A pattern matches the directory it names and everything beneath it, and PowerShell wildcards work: \\FS01\*\Archive covers every share on a server. Excluding anything makes the run incremental, so it reconciles nothing.
$comment_includePaths: UNC path patterns restricting which directories are reported. The walk still passes through the directories between a root and a match - it has to, to reach them - and reports none of them, so a reported directory whose parent was passed over carries boundary_reason 'parent_unreadable'. Setting this makes the run incremental.
$comment_reparsePointPolicy: What to do at a junction or symlink. 'skip' (the default) reads its own descriptor - it
is a real directory with a real ACL - and does not descend, because what lies below it
belongs to the target and is reported under the target's own path. 'ignore' does not read
it at all. 'follow' descends, guarded by the reparse targets already crossed on that
branch: a junction whose target the branch has crossed before is read and not followed,
because a visited-path set cannot catch that cycle - every trip round it produces a path
nothing has seen. Any of the three leaves paths under the junction unreported, so a tree
$comment_concurrencyLimit: How many descriptor reads may be in flight at once. Reading a security descriptor over SMB is almost entirely latency, so 8 to 16 is a large win against a remote file server and none at all against a local disk. It changes throughput only: the walk's decisions stay sequential and its output is identical at every setting.
$comment_timeoutSeconds: Stop after this long, write a checkpoint, and report the run as 'canceled'. 0 is no limit. A scan that runs out of time never reports the part it reached as the whole; setting this makes the run incremental, so it reconciles nothing.
$comment_includeFiles: Read the DACL of every file as well as every directory. Off by default and expensive: an estate holds orders of magnitude more files than directories, and this turns a scan measured in minutes into one measured in days. A file is never traversed, and it is compared against the object projection of its directory rather than the container one.
$comment_checkpointPath: Where to record the frontier so an interrupted scan can be resumed with -Resume. Leave empty to disable checkpointing. The file holds pending directories and the parent facts each needs to judge its own boundary - no observations, and no credentials. Resuming is refused if the roots, depth, patterns, reparse policy, or file setting have changed since it was written.
$comment_reportUnresolvedPrincipals: Emit a principal observation for every trustee SID that did not resolve to a name. Leave it on: an orphaned SID on a folder ACL is one of the findings this tool exists to produce, and the backend cannot infer it from the ACE alone.
